newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-MOORE SENT OFF AS SALE SNATCH LATE WIN.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-MOORE SENT OFF AS SALE SNATCH LATE WIN.

text.p: Former England and British Lions hooker Brian Moore was sent off for the first time since 1984 on Saturday as his side Richmond lost 34-30 to Sale in the fifth round of the Pilkington Cup, English rugby's domestic knock-out competition.

With Richmond leading 30-21, Moore was dismissed on the hour for stamping by referee Chris White and, in a pulsating finale, the first division outfit Sale came from behind to beat the second division big-spenders.
Moore could now face a two-month ban although, as a qualified solicitor, he is ready to fight any suspension.

"I don't think it was even worth a penalty," he said. "I was incredulous when he showed me the card. I was driving forward with the ball in my hand into a maul. Other players collapsed the maul and I kept driving over them.
"In somewhere like New Zealand the player on the ground would have been penalised. I certainly did not put my foot on anybody above their shoulder height.
"Obviously I feel bad that we lost the game and that my sending-off must have played a part, because we had only 14 men. But my offence was nominal and in that sense I don't feel comfortable."

Meanwhile, cup holders Bath, without their injured England pair of Phil de Glanville and Mike Catt, began their defence at this stage with a convincing 33-0 win over London Irish at the Recreation Ground. Another England man, Jeremy Guscott, produced the individual performance of the day with a hat-trick of tries in 13 minutes in the only all-first division tie.

In contrast, last year's losing finalists, Leicester, who currently top the first division, were made to fight all the way by fourth division Newbury. Leicester took the opportunity to rest a number of regular first team members including their internationals and the plan almost backfired as they squeezed into the last 16 by 26-21.

Another first division team Orrell were taken to extra-time before scraping home 34-31 against second division Bedford. Orrell, bottom of the first division, had their New Zealand back row forward Richard Higgs sent off for fighting eight minutes into the second half, and only a late penalty allowed them to finish the 80 minutes at 19-19.
Bedford then got an early score through rugby league international Martin Offiah but Orrell finished strongly to make it through to the next round.
The other first division sides all progressed comfortably with Wasps the day's biggest winners when they beat Rugby 84-8.
